claim: ruff S603 (subprocess untrusted input) at updater.py:595,598,600,967
rationale: All flagged subprocess.run() calls use list-form argv (never shell=True), with hardcoded command names (dbus-send, systemctl, bash) and locally-generated paths (tempfile, ENGINE resolved next to updater.py). No user-controlled input flows into any argv, so shell/command injection is not reachable. S603 fires on every subprocess call regardless of actual risk; safe for this desktop GUI.

claim: ruff S607 (partial executable path) at updater.py:629,652,653,656,663,967
rationale: Flags use of bare tool names (systemctl, dbus-send, bash) resolved via PATH. These are standard trusted system binaries for a Linux desktop app; using absolute paths would be non-portable across distros. No attacker-controlled PATH is in scope (single-user desktop session). Intended behaviour, not a lookalike-binary risk.

claim: shellcheck SC2001 at update_system.sh:267 (use ${//} instead of sed)
rationale: The sed is `echo "$dupe" | sed 's/^/      /'` which prefixes every line of a multi-line variable using the per-line ^ anchor. Bash ${var//search/replace} cannot match a line-start anchor across multiple lines, so sed is the correct tool here, not a stylistic slip. No change warranted.

claim: pyright/mypy (~32) "type[Qt] has no attribute AlignVCenter / QProcess.MergedChannels / bytes(QByteArray)"
rationale: These are PySide6 type-stub scoping gaps, not runtime bugs. Short-form enum access (Qt.AlignVCenter, Qt.PointingHandCursor, QProcess.MergedChannels) and bytes(QByteArray) are all valid and work at runtime in PySide6/Qt6; the bundled .pyi stubs just don't expose them at that scope. No pyproject/type-check config exists in the project, so these are not gating CI. Suppress unless the project adopts fully-scoped enum idioms project-wide.

claim: tests/run-tests.sh:1360 — isolation defect via a shell-out (pre-pass pattern `system_shell_out`)
rationale: Line 1360 is a plain banner: echo "TEST: a non-English locale still detects an up-to-date system (LC_ALL pinned)". The pattern is looking for C's system() call and matched the literal substring "system (" inside English prose. No shell-out, no engine call, no export at or near that line; the scenario below it goes through run_engine normally. Pattern is language-inappropriate for a .sh file, where system() cannot occur.

claim: tests/bump-test.py:95 and tests/docs-check.py:230 — error_handling defect at the final exit (pre-pass pattern `cpp_exit`)
rationale: Both lines are `sys.exit(main())`, the correct Python idiom for propagating a status code. bump-test.py:91 returns `1 if failed else 0`; docs-check.py:226 returns `1 if failures else 0`. Nothing is swallowed — the exit code faithfully reflects the tally. The pattern is aimed at C/C++ `exit()` calls buried mid-test and does not apply to a module's `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard.

claim: tests/gui-smoke.py:57 and :1361 — error_handling defect at exit (pre-pass pattern `cpp_exit`)
rationale: Line 57 is `sys.exit(77)` on ImportError — the documented skip-for-absent-tool convention (77 is read as "skipped" by local-CI.sh:38-44 and .github/workflows/release.yml:33, all three verified to agree). Line 1361 is `sys.exit(code)` where code is `1 if FAIL else 0`. Neither swallows a failure; both are the intended exit-code contract described in docs/standards/testing.md §1.

claim: tests/gui-smoke.py:89 — flakiness from a fixed sleep (pre-pass patterns `sleep_call` / `posix_sleep`)
rationale: The `time.sleep(0.02)` at :89 is the body of `_wait_for_notify`'s poll loop (`while time.monotonic() < deadline`), i.e. the poll-with-timeout pattern the standard prescribes — not a blind sleep guessing a duration. On timeout it returns False, so the caller's check() goes red rather than green. A separate, narrower residual risk (the 2.0s deadline racing a real subprocess spawn) is recorded as its own LOW finding rather than as this pattern hit.

claim: mypy (68 of 229): "type[Qt]/type[QMessageBox]/type[QProcess] has no attribute X" and "No overload variant of bytes matches QByteArray"
rationale: PySide6 shorthand enum access (Qt.UserRole, QMessageBox.Ok, QProcess.MergedChannels, Qt.NoBrush) is valid at runtime; the bundled stubs model only the scoped form. bytes(QByteArray) likewise works via the buffer protocol. Verified at oneup/gui/auth.py:92-170, rollback.py:57/85/161, toggle_switch.py:113, app_update.py:37/68. The GUI smoke suite exercises all of these paths green. Same class already recorded in this ledger on 2026-08-19 as "~32"; the count grew with the v2 package split, not the defect.

claim: mypy union-attr (20): ".parent() has no attribute auto_btn/..." in settings_dialog.py:120-122, and "QCoreApplication | None expected QApplication" at window.py:733/753
rationale: Both are narrowings mypy cannot prove and that hold by construction. SettingsDialog is only ever constructed with the main window as parent (focus_chain reads p.auto_btn etc., all defined on Updater); QApplication.instance() cannot be None while a QWidget slot is executing, which is the only route to window.py:733/753. No runtime defect: the GUI smoke suite drives Settings, the theme picker and the contrast toggle green. A real fix here means an assert or a cast, which is type ceremony rather than a behaviour change.

claim: mypy (14): variable-reuse and tuple-arity in theme.py:70/79/94/102/142/143/183/883/1019/1039/1196, proc.py:67/76, run.py:580/615
rationale: Three checker limitations, none a runtime defect. (a) A name rebound to a different type after the first branch returns — proc.py:67 rebinds `completed` only after the stream branch returned at :65; theme.py:142 rebinds `fill` from tuple to str via _hex(); run.py:580/615 rebind n/total right after an .isdigit() guard. (b) A generator comprehension yields tuple[int, ...] where a fixed-arity tuple is declared (theme.py:70/94/102/883/1039). (c) _samples(*stops) unpacks a known 2-element list into (a, b, n=101); mypy cannot prove the length, so it binds the list to n. theme.py:1196 is QSettings.value() typed object in the stubs despite type=float. All verified by reading each site.

claim: mypy (4): "Item None of IO[str] | None has no attribute __iter__" at proc.py:231, and "Path | None" at steps.py:372/390/403
rationale: proc.py:231 iterates child.stdout inside stream_filtered, whose Popen at :207 passes stdout=subprocess.PIPE unconditionally — typeshed does not narrow Popen.stdout from the constructor argument. steps.py's _SYS_LOG is declared `Path | None = None` at module level and assigned `Path(path)` at :630, two lines before the only call to _system_upgrade() at :632; every use at :372/:390/:403 is reachable only through that call. Deferred module-level init is unprovable to a checker, not a None deref. Note the sibling _SYS_LOG_FIRST IS guarded at :485, because that one can genuinely still be None.

claim: bandit B103 + B108 and semgrep insecure-file-permissions, all at tests/gui-smoke.py:45 and :1326
rationale: Both sites are deliberate test scaffolding and both already carry the equivalent ruff suppression with its reason. :45 chmods 0o755 on a generated PATH mock — a mock the suite puts on PATH must be executable, and it is written into a per-run temp dir (`# noqa: S103`). :1326 passes the string "/tmp/x.log" to tray._tray_check_args purely as an argument value to assert on; nothing opens it (`# noqa: S108 — an argument value, never opened`). The semgrep hit at :45 is the same finding as bandit B103, reported twice by two tools.

The Popen is a fixed argv list with no shell: [sys.executable, "-c", _KEEPALIVE_SRC, KEEPALIVE_TAG, str(os.getpid()), interval]. _KEEPALIVE_SRC and KEEPALIVE_TAG are module constants, the pid is os.getpid(), and `interval` is the only environment-derived element — validated on the line immediately above by KEEPALIVE_SECONDS.replace(".","",1).isdigit(), falling back to "50". shlex.quote() is inapplicable because there is no shell to quote for. The site already carries `# noqa: S603` with the same reasoning, matching the engine-wide convention in security.md §2.2.

claim: shellcheck SC2001 [style] at update_system.sh:1340 — "see if you can use ${variable//search/replace} instead"
rationale: The line is `echo "$dupe" | sed 's/^/      /'`, which prefixes SIX SPACES TO EVERY LINE of a multi-line variable. Bash parameter expansion has no per-line anchored form, so the suggested ${var//x/y} replacement cannot express this at all — it would have to match the empty string at every position, not at each line start. The tool is pattern-matching on `sed 's/.../.../'` without reading the anchor. This ledger already carries the same rule dismissed at update_system.sh:267 on 2026-08-19; the engine rewrite moved the line, not the reasoning.

claim: typos (193 of 203): 145 inside two PNG binaries, plus 'ba'/'ede' in git SHAs, 'sytem' as a deliberate example, and 'nam'/'pn' as identifiers
rationale: Four classes, none a misspelling. (a) 145 hits are byte sequences inside screenshots/oneup.png and oneup-light.png — binary files typos should never have been fed; screenshots/ is absent from the default exclusion set, which names static/images/ instead. (b) 'ba' x7 and 'ede' x1 fall inside abbreviated commit hashes such as `03435ba` and `b3ede2d`. (c) 'sytem' x6 is the DELIBERATE typo example for --steps validation, at oneup/engine/__main__.py:155, update_system.sh:383 and the ONEUP-0054 plan quoting them. (d) 'nam' x3 is win._nam, the conventional Qt abbreviation for QNetworkAccessManager, and 'pn' x3 is a local counter in tests/run-tests.sh. The remaining 10 'mis' hits are the standing hyphenated-prefix calibration.

claim: vulture: unused variable 'tz' at tests/gui-smoke.py:1703, and yamllint truthy at .github/workflows/release.yml:5
rationale: Both are required by an external contract. 'tz' is the parameter of a `def now(cls, tz=None)` classmethod standing in for datetime.now(); the parameter must exist, and may be passed by keyword, so it cannot be renamed or dropped without breaking the stub's compatibility with the API it mocks. The yamllint truthy hit is on GitHub Actions' `on:` key, which YAML 1.1 reads as a boolean — it is the workflow schema's mandatory key name and cannot be spelled any other way; this is yamllint's best-known false positive on Actions files.
